facts.text: Waterford earned its name from Waterford, Ireland, where some of its founders once lived before immigrating to the United States.
In 1970, the entire village and surrounding farmland were declared a National Historic Landmark District, the highest U.S. historic designation.
The Waterford Foundation, founded over 75 years ago, preserves the village’s historic buildings and open spaces through education and stewardship.
The Second Street School, built in 1867, was the first one‑room African‑American schoolhouse in Waterford, funded by the Freedmen’s Bureau and Quaker support.
Waterford’s annual fair, called “An Autumn Celebration of Americana,” showcases historic homes, artisan crafts, live music, and living history exhibits.
The Phillips Farm Trail Network invites visitors to explore Waterford’s natural side, winding through preserved farmland and historic landscapes.
